title: Personal Portfolio — Full Technical Overview
text:
This is Ikeoluwa Oladele's personal portfolio site, built from scratch as both a showcase and a technical project in its own right. It consists of two independently deployable parts: a Vue 3 single-page application for the frontend and a Python FastAPI backend deployed as an Azure Functions V2 app.

The most distinctive feature is the AI chatbot embedded in the bottom-right corner of every page. It is context-aware — when a visitor is browsing a specific project, the bot knows which project is in focus and can answer questions about it specifically. The chatbot uses a RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipeline: incoming questions are first checked against a topic gate (a Pinecone index seeded with representative questions, scored with a reranker), and only on-topic questions proceed to retrieval. Retrieval fans out across all project namespaces in Pinecone using the multilingual-e5-large integrated embedding model, then re-ranks the combined results with pinecone-rerank-v0. The top results are passed as context to Google Gemini (gemini-flash-lite) for generation.

Project data is pulled live from GitHub. Any public repository belonging to TheBluCoder and tagged with the 'portfolio' GitHub topic is automatically ingested into Pinecone. Each repo's README and optional .github/project.json metadata file are fetched, chunked, and stored in a namespace named github:TheBluCoder:<repo-name>. A GitHub webhook triggers re-ingestion on push, and removes namespaces when a repo is deleted or privatised. Additional context that does not fit in a README can be manually uploaded through the admin API endpoint POST /api/admin/projects/{repo}/context.

The frontend is built with Vue 3, Vite, and Tailwind CSS v4. Pages include a home/introduction section, an about page, a projects browser, a gallery, and a resume page. The projects page fetches live data from the backend and falls back to a static JSON file when the API is unavailable. The chat panel maintains separate conversation histories per project. Markdown in chat responses is rendered with markdown-it.

The backend uses FastAPI with Pydantic for validation. It is deployed using Azure Functions V2's AsgiMiddleware, which wraps the FastAPI ASGI app without requiring any code changes between local and cloud environments. Storage uses Azure Table Storage for the gallery (poems, comments, likes), reading list, and rate-limit counters, with in-process memory fallback for local development. Rate limiting is set to 12 requests per 60 seconds per visitor fingerprint (IP + User-Agent hash).

The resume page parses a PDF hosted on Google Drive using pdfplumber, then sends the extracted text to Gemini to produce a structured JSON object (experience, education, skills, about). The parsed result is cached in-process for 24 hours; the admin can flush it via DELETE /api/admin/resume/cache to force a re-parse after updating the PDF.

The gallery section displays poems written by Ikeoluwa, supports likes (anonymous, one per visitor session) and comments (moderated — comments appear only after admin approval). The admin dashboard at /admin allows managing poems, moderating comments, editing the reading list, and flushing the resume cache.

Ikeoluwa is a student at Algonquin College studying computer science. This portfolio demonstrates skills in full-stack development, AI/ML integration, cloud deployment (Azure), vector databases (Pinecone), and API design. The project is intentionally built with production-quality patterns: proper rate limiting, HMAC-verified webhooks, dual-mode storage with graceful fallbacks, and a clean separation between the Azure Functions entry point and the core FastAPI application.
